newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas falls on prompt, little changed further.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas falls on prompt, little changed further.

text.p: UK spot natural gas prices were little changed in quiet trade on Tuesday, traders and brokers said, with only the day ahead market showing much movement as levels slipped.
Day ahead prices are closely linked to activity on the flexibility mechanism, which in turn dictates the System Average Price (SAP), published daily and also as a 7-day and a 30-day rolling average.

There was a flexibility mechanism system buy on Monday at a marginal price of 0.4422 pence per kiloWatt hour, or 12.96 pence a therm. The SAP had gone up to 0.4397 p/kWh (12.89 pence a therm), boosting the day ahead price on Monday for Tuesday.

But with the SAP coming off on Tuesday, day ahead prices for Wednesday also tracked back. Trade was heard as low as 11.175 pence a therm, compared with deals at up to 11.75 pence a therm the previous day.
Further forward, the market was quiet. A trader said that early in the morning prices had come off before moving back later in the afternoon, but the net result was that few changes were seen.

There were trades seen in the fourth quarter at 13.50 pence a therm twice. There were rumours that the buyer of one of these was also the buyer of a Q1 piece at 16.80 pence a therm, and also of a 25,000 th/d lot for summer 1998 - which was not confirmed done - at 11.25 pence a therm.
If correct, this would mean the player had effectively bought the 1997 gas year at 13.20 pence a therm, roughly in line with the closing assessment of 13.00/13.15 pence a therm.
There were also rumours that a trade was done in the third quarter for weekdays only, but no details emerged and the deal remained unconfirmed.

The market has been relatively stable at a new, lower price range since Friday, when prices came down sharply. One of the reasons widely cited at the time for the fall was the expectation of an announcement in Enron's North Sea disputes concerning J-Block and the CATS system.

Both of these have now been resolved, sending signals which dealers perceived as bearish to the market. But the market has taken the J-Block settlement and the CATS judgment in its stride, with prices hardly moving so far this week.
IPE futures were barely traded, with only two lots done. Both July and September were traded at firmer prices, which one futures broker said "doesn't sit consistently with the OTC market."
